name: After Effects
category: A7. Native applications and procedural tools
role: Adobe's aerender CLI and ExtendScript render existing .aep projects and templates
summary: Adobe's commercial motion-graphics app. aerender renders an existing .aep project or template headlessly, a frame range to an image sequence or movie, and ExtendScript or the app can swap text and footage into a template first. Its strength is that designers' existing AE templates render without rebuilding them. No source, no Linux, and every render needs an Adobe licence.
use_when: A designer's .aep template must render with swapped text or footage
Over Blender when the look depends on AE effects or plugins
Over Natron when the project already exists as .aep
Compositing with third-party AE plugins that have no native equivalent
avoid_when: Building new motion from scratch: Blender, GSAP or Manim need no licence
Unattended or CI renders without a seat: Natron or Blender
Rendering on machines where Adobe cannot be installed or signed in
license: Proprietary, Adobe Creative Cloud subscription required; aerender ships with the app
notes: 2026-10-26: Adobe help page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so the version, release date and licence terms for command-line rendering were not read; verify on the machine. aerender is inside the app folder, not on PATH.

assessment.rationale: Adobe's help page returned HTTP 403, so current version and release date were not verified. Commercial and subscription-only, but the only route to render existing .aep templates; no open neighbour reads the format.
